episode_title: Episode 96: Lucy Pimblott of The Wellness Lounge, Leeds

real_qa.q: Why did Lucy Pimblott choose to focus The Wellness Lounge Leeds exclusively on wellness-related businesses?
real_qa.r: Lucy prioritizes wellness because she was diagnosed with breast cancer three years ago and believes in self-advocacy of personal health. She wanted to create a space that reflects her values around supporting wellness practitioners like yoga instructors, pilates teachers, beauticians, and menopause wellness specialists. Her daughter is a beautician, which also informed her awareness that independent practitioners needed high-end commercial spaces with proper amenities like hot and cold running water and room for multiple treatments.
real_qa.requete: Why The Wellness Lounge Leeds wellness focus

real_qa.q: How did Lucy Pimblott acquire the building for The Wellness Lounge Leeds when she initially thought it was unaffordable?
real_qa.r: Lucy discovered that a former Halifax bank building on Garforth Main Street was for sale. Because it was for sale rather than to let, and the banks wanted to know how the property would be used, she had to write a competitive bid explaining her vision of creating a hub for small businesses and community spaces. She wrote a bid telling the sellers what she planned to do with the premises, which was different from a standard commercial transaction focused on profit.
real_qa.requete: How Lucy Pimblott bought former Halifax bank building Leeds

real_qa.q: What contract length does The Wellness Lounge Leeds offer to allow practitioners to try the space without long-term commitment?
real_qa.r: The Wellness Lounge Leeds offers an initial short contract of 16 weeks, which is long enough for practitioners to properly try the space but short enough that they don't over-commit themselves. This is in contrast to standard commercial leases of three to five years with 18-month break clauses, which Lucy felt would deter independent practitioners from renting.
real_qa.requete: Wellness Lounge Leeds 16 week contract trial

real_qa.q: What approach did Lucy Pimblott take when she was prescribed tamoxifen and AI inhibitors for breast cancer treatment?
real_qa.r: Lucy did not simply follow standard medical advice. She tried tamoxifen but found it made her depressed, so she stopped it. When offered AI inhibitors (anastrozole) after a preventative hysterectomy, she declined and had a full conversation with her oncologist, explaining she was not prepared to risk her mental health for a small percentage benefit. She emphasizes the importance of self-advocacy and listening to your own body rather than blindly following standard medical protocols.
real_qa.requete: Lucy Pimblott tamoxifen AI inhibitors breast cancer treatment

real_qa.q: What was Lucy Pimblott's market insight that led to creating The Wellness Lounge Leeds?
real_qa.r: Lucy identified a significant gap in the marketplace for high-end commercial spaces available on a flexible, part-time basis. Many independent beauty therapists and wellness practitioners needed affordable rental options because their businesses were part-time, side hustles, or they were still training. Full-time monthly rents were too expensive for practitioners who only needed space for a day a week, so Lucy created a model allowing practitioners to rent space flexibly rather than committing to full-time occupancy.
real_qa.requete: Wellness Lounge Leeds part-time flexible space independent practitioners

guest.bio_context: Lucy Pimblott is the owner and founder of The Wellness Lounge Leeds, a high-end coworking space for independent wellness practitioners located on Garforth Main Street in Leeds. She was previously a bid manager with experience writing construction bids. She was diagnosed with breast cancer three years ago at age 47, which became a driving force behind her mission to create supportive spaces for small wellness businesses and practitioners.
